Plaintiff, Jalissa Blackwood, by and through undersigned counsel, hereby avers as follows:.

sections.name: INTRODUCTION
sentences: Plaintiff has initiated this action to redress violations by Reliance Family Care Services, Inc. d/b/a Reliance Family Care (“Reliance”), Uwayemen Uwadiale (“Uwadiale”), and Regan Ataman (“Ataman”) (collectively “Defendants”) of Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 (“Title VI’- 42 U.S.C. § 2000e ef seg.), 42 U.S.C. §1981 (“Section 1981”), the Pennsylvania Case 2:25-cv-07221-MMB Document1- Filed 12/22/25 Page 2 of 14 Human Relations Act (“PHRA” — 43 PS. § 951 ef seg.), and the Philadelphia Fair Practices Ordinance (“PFPO” — Phila.
Code § 9-1100 ef seq.).' Plaintiff was unlawfully terminated by Defendants and has suffered damages more fully described/sought herein.

sections.name: JURISDICTION AND VENUE
sentences: This Court, in accordance with 28 U.S.C. § 1331, has jurisdiction over Plaintiff's claims because this civil action arises under laws of the United States.

This Court may properly maintain personal jurisdiction over each Defendant because each Defendant’s contacts with this state and this judicial district are sufficient for the exercise of jurisdiction over each Defendant to comply with traditional notions of fair play and substantial justice, satisfying the standard set forth by the Supreme Court of the United States in International Shoe Co. v. Washington, 326 U.S. 310 (1945) and its progeny.

Pursuant to 28 U.S.C. § 1391(b)(1) and (b)(2), venue is properly laid in this district because all of the acts and/or omissions giving rise to the claims set forth herein occurred in this judicial district.

sentences: The foregoing paragraphs are incorporated herein in their entirety as if set forth in full.
Plaintiff is an adult individual, with an address as set forth in the caption.
' Plaintiff identifies that she will pursue PHRA/PFPO claims herein for notice purposes only.
She omits such claims in the Count Section of this Complaint.
Plaintiff will move to amend the instant lawsuit to include PHRA/PFPO claims upon completion of administrative exhaustion (or waiver of exhaustion by Defendants).

Case 2:25-cv-07221-MMB Document1 = Filed 12/22/25 Page 3 of 14 Defendant Reliance Family Care Services, Inc. is believed and therefore averred to be a domestic Pennsylvania corporation with principal place of business at the above-captioned address.
Reliance engages in the business of providing residential rehabilitation and in-home and community services for individuals with intellectual disabilities.
Reliance employed at least one hundred (100) employees during Plaintiff's employment with Defendants.

Defendant Uwayemen Uwadiale is believed and therefore averred to be an individual employed at the above-captioned address. | Uwadiale is believed and therefore averred to be a citizen of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania residing within the Eastern District of Pennsylvania.
Defendant Regan Ataman is believed and therefore averred to be an individual employed at the above-captioned address.

Ataman is believed and therefore averred to be a citizen of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania residing within the Eastern District of Pennsylvania. | Uwadiale and Ataman may be held individually liable in this action consistent with Section 1981 and precedent noted herein. | Uwadiale and Ataman are believed and therefore averred to be husband and wife.

At all times relevant herein, each Defendant acted by and through its agents, servants and employees, each of whom acted at all times relevant herein in the course and scope of their employment with and for Defendant.
Case 2:25-cv-07221-MMB Document1- Filed 12/22/25 Page 4 of 14.

sections.name: FACTUAL BACKGROUND
sentences: The foregoing paragraphs are incorporated herein in their entirety as if set forth in full.

Plaintiff is African American. | Upon information and belief, Uwadiale (African) was at all relevant times the Chief Operating Officer (“COO”) and Executive Director of Reliance. | Upon information and belief, Ataman (African) was at all relevant times the Chief Executive Officer (“CEO”) and President of Reliance.
In or around April 2023, Plaintiff was hired by Reliance as a Direct Support Worker.
Plaintiff was employed with Reliance as a DSP for almost two (2) years, until on or about March 27, 2025.
Plaintiff's job duties as a DSP included supervising her clients’ daily life activities, such as cooking, cleaning, taking medication, and attending doctor’s appointments.
Plaintiff was an exemplary employee and she worked very hard for Reliance.

Plaintiff was supervised by Scheduling Coordinator Magnus Connor (African American, “Connor’), Scheduler Blessing Olaseinde (African, “Olaseinde”), DSP Supervisor Kanda Kiawu (African, “Kiawu”), and DSP Supervisor Patience Abalo (African, “Abalo”).
Plaintiff worked as a DSP for two (2) separate shifts to assist Reliance (an enterprise that is often short staffed).
Plaintiff worked approximately thirty-six (36) hours per week.

Case 2:25-cv-07221-MMB Document1- Filed 12/22/25 Page 5 of 14 At the time of her separation, Plaintiff generally worked eight (8) hour shifts on Monday and Tuesday (11:00pm to 7:00am) and a sixteen (16) hour shift beginning on Wednesday at 11:00pm and ending on Thursday at 3:00pm.
On or about Wednesday March 26, 2025 to Thursday March 27, 2025, Plaintiff was working a double shift that was scheduled for sixteen (16) hours.
Plaintiffs sixteen (16) hour double shift was scheduled to end at or around 3:00pm.
Defendant’s DSP Sadia (last name unknown) (African, “Sadia”) was scheduled to relieve Plaintiff at 3:00pm.
Obviously, for safety reasons, a person providing care should not continue working when too fatigued or exhausted.
This is in addition to other obligations Plaintiff had. Before Plaintiff was to leave, Sadia told Plaintiff that she was going to be approximately two (2) hours late to relieve Plaintiff.
Plaintiff responded that she could not work past 3:00pm.
Plaintiff went to Kiawu and told her about this situation.
Kiawu shrugged off Plaintiff's concerns and told her to speak to Connor.
Plaintiff then went to discuss this matter with Connor, who told Plaintiff that Sadia had to come into work at 3:00pm.
Plaintiff complained to Connor that “they” (meaning the African employees) were sticking together and that “we” (meaning the Non-African employees) were being treated worse than them by Reliance.
Connor told Olaseinde that Sadia had to relieve Plaintiff at 3:00pm, but Olaseinde just laughed and did not relay this message to Sadia.

Case 2:25-cv-07221-MMB Document1- Filed 12/22/25 Page 6 of 14 At or around 1:00pm on this date, Plaintiffs client had a seizure and needed to be taken to the hospital. _ Plaintiff went to talk to Ataman, with Kiawu present, about Sadia saying that she would be two (2) hours late to relieve Plaintiff.
Plaintiff told Ataman that she was not trying to get anyone in trouble, but that it was her second shift and Sadia was supposed to relieve her at 3:00pm.
Ataman told Plaintiff that Sadia needed to start her shift at 3:00pm.
Ataman told Plaintiff to tell Sadia that she had to go with Plaintiff's client to the hospital.
Ataman also told Plaintiff that she could finish out her shift with Sadia’s client.
After the meeting, Olaseinde started yelling at Plaintiff that Sadia would not be going to the hospital because she needed to pick up her child.
But, Sadia had already signed up to work at 3:00pm.

Plaintiff did not understand why Sadia did not have to come in at 3:00pm because she had signed up for that shift. _ Olaseinde told Plaintiff to put her client’s medication at his apartment and that another DSP would go with her client to the hospital.

Plaintiff took her client’s medication to his apartment and put it away safely. | When Plaintiff attempted to clock out at the end of her shift, Plaintiff noticed that she had already been clocked out. When Plaintiff tried to find out why she had been clocked out, Plaintiff was accused of being unprofessional, that she abandoned her patient, that she did not go to the emergency room when she was supposed to go, and that she would need to sign a write up. Case 2:25-cv-07221-MMB Document1- Filed 12/22/25 Page 7 of 14 This was all false, and none of it was an accurate portrayal of anything that actually transpired.
Plaintiff was never again permitted to work and thus effectively terminated on March 27, 2025.
Plaintiff was never permitted to work after March 27, 2025, nor was she rescheduled to work.
Plaintiff called continually (for weeks) to find out her employment status and to understand what had gone on, but no one answered Plaintiff’ s questions.
Plaintiff was terminated for: (a) working 16 hours; (b) leaving at the end of her shift; and, (c) doing so with permission from Ataman.
Plaintiff did nothing wrong, let alone anything warranting discipline. | Most of the managers and employees at Reliance are from Africa (and African), including Uwadiale and Ataman.
Virtually all of Plaintiff's management was African.
Anyone who was not African at Reliance was abused, exploited, terminated for petty reasons, and there was immense disparate treatment towards non-A fricans in that workplace.

The unequal treatment was blatant and Africans were not terminated for significant (actual) performance problems or misconduct whereas Non-African employees were terminated for engaging in the same or similar conduct.
Other Non-African employees have brought cases against Reliance for this very reason.
A prior manager named Bill (Faye) Lane pursued a legal claim against Defendants wherein he outlined extensive examples of discrimination based upon race / national origin against Non-Africans.

Case 2:25-cv-07221-MMB Document1- Filed 12/22/25 Page 8 of 14 Other staff members such as Luvenia Ross-Thompson and Charde Earley pursued legal claims against Defendants outlining extensive discrimination against Non-Africans.
Numerous former employees provided witness declarations of blatant discrimination against non-Africans. = If Plaintiff were African, Plaintiff would not have been terminated.
Plaintiff constantly complained to her coworkers about how Reliance treated non- African employees worse than African employees.
Defendants retaliated against Plaintiff and terminated her because of her good faith complaints of discrimination based on race/national origin.

Plaintiff believes she was singled out for termination because of her race and/or national origin; furthermore, Plaintiff believes that her concerns of institutional race/national origin discrimination were also a determinative factor in her termination from employment.
Plaintiff was pretextually terminated because of her race, national origin and/or her engagement in protected activity.

sections.name: COUNTI
sentences: Violation of Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, as amended [1] Race / National Origin Discrimination and [2] Retaliation -Against Defendant Reliance Only- The foregoing paragraphs are incorporated herein in their entirety as if set forth in full.
Plaintiff was subjected to disparate treatment because of her race and/or national origin.
Plaintiff was also subjected to disparate treatment because she engaged in protected activity by complaining about disparate treatment based on her race and/or national origin.

Case 2:25-cv-07221-MMB Document1- Filed 12/22/25 Page 9 of 14 Plaintiff believes and therefore avers that she was terminated pretextually because of her race and/or national origin and in retaliation for engaging in protected activity.

sections.name: COUNT II
sentences: Violation of 42 U.S.C. §1981 [1] Race / National Origin Discrimination and [2] Retaliation -Against All Defendants- The foregoing paragraphs are incorporated herein in their entirety as if set forth in full.
Plaintiff was subjected to disparate treatment because of her race and/or national origin.
Plaintiff was also subjected to disparate treatment because she engaged in protected activity by complaining about disparate treatment based on her race and/or national origin.
Plaintiff believes and therefore avers that she was terminated pretextually because of her race and/or national origin and in retaliation for engaging in protected activity.
Consistent with Sheridan v. E.Plaintiff.

DuPont de Nemours and Co., 100 F.3d 1061, 1077-78 (3d Cir.1996) (en banc) and its progeny, an individual may be subject to liability under § 1981 when the individual intentionally causes an infringement of rights protected by Section 1981, regardless of whether the employer may also be held liable.
See a/so Al-Khazraji v. Saint Francis Coll., 784 F.2d 505, 518 (3d Cir. 1986); Santiago v. City of Vineland, 107 F.Supp.2d 512, 540-41 (D.N.J.2000); Shaw v. Temple Univ., 357 F. Supp.

At all times relevant herein, Uwadiale and Ataman were personally involved in the discrimination and retaliation against Plaintiff and/or intentionally caused Reliance to infringe upon her rights under §1981.
These actions as aforesaid constitute violations of §1981.
Case 2:25-cv-07221-MMB Documenti1- Filed 12/22/25 Page 10 of 14 Plaintiff has suffered damages as set forth more fully herein.

WHEREFORE, Plaintiff prays that this Court enter an Order providing that: Defendant is to promulgate and adhere to a policy prohibiting discrimination in the future against any employee(s); Defendant is to compensate Plaintiff, reimburse Plaintiff, and make Plaintiff whole for any and all pay and benefits Plaintiff would have received had it not been for Defendant’s illegal actions, including but not limited to back pay, front pay, salary, pay increases, bonuses, insurance, benefits, training, promotions, reinstatement and seniority; Plaintiff is to be awarded liquidated damages and/or punitive damages as appropriate, as permitted by applicable law, in an amount believed by the Court or trier of fact to be appropriate to punish Defendant for its willful, deliberate, malicious and outrageous conduct and to deter Defendant or other employers from engaging in such misconduct in the future; Plaintiff is to be accorded other equitable and legal relief as the Court deems just, proper and appropriate (including but not limited to damages for emotional distress, pain, suffering and humiliation); Plaintiff is to be awarded the costs and expenses of this action and reasonable attorney’s fees as provided by applicable federal and state law; and Plaintiff demands trial by jury on all issues so triable pursuant to Fed.R.Civ.P.
